query:
I travel every week with a Realme X7 Pro and a USB-C laptop. The frozen phone listing says a 65 W charger is included and advertises a full charge in 35 minutes. I would like one travel brick, but a previous phone battery swelled after two years of nightly fast charging, so verified compatibility matters more than the largest printed wattage.

Compare all four named routes: keep realme included 65w phone charger and separate laptop brick; buy cirtek 100w multiport route after realme protocol and port checks; buy ugreen 65w single port pd route for verified pd devices; and defer universal brick pending realme protocol temperature and load test.

Treat these as hard constraints: advertised wattage is not delivered device power; phone charger cable and protocol must all match; one brick must support laptop and phone use case; simultaneous port allocation must be audited; seller safety and battery life claims are not longitudinal tests; heat and charge controls require system specific evidence; owner reports are scoped anecdotes not causal tests; usb c shape is not protocol or wattage guarantee; and suspicious price and small review displays must be preserved.

Audit the complete frozen Realme X7 Pro, Cirtek 100 W, and UGREEN 65 W product bodies, including exact price and review displays, box contents, port counts, named protocols, cable requirements, listed devices, single-port limits, and simultaneous allocations. Explain how the Quick Charge, USB-C, charger-control, battery-management, and lithium-ion material changes what can and cannot be concluded. Reconcile the charging-speed, 5 W, temperature-hold, and fast-charge explainer discussions without transferring a different owner's outcome to this Realme. Specify a bounded screen-off trial for the phone and laptop in every intended single-device and simultaneous-port setup, including negotiated indicators, charge interval, interruptions, and temperature warnings. Then recommend one route or defer, preserving every seller, owner, price, review, protocol, compatibility, temperature, safety, and missing longitudinal-measurement limitation.
